#2598. Nets can’t overcome slow start in 129-110 loss to Grizzlies

Those are words you never want to hear from the head coach of a rebuilding team. Especially not in Year 3.

The Brooklyn Nets had a chance to build on their blowout win over New Orleans. Mikel Brown Jr. was back after missing the last two games. There was a small window to finally pick up some momentum. Instead, they followed it up with another frustrating loss, 129-110, in the finale of a four-game road-trip.

Brooklyn fell behind early and trailed 38-23 after the first quarter. You'd never think Memphis played a game just the night before.

The Nets struggled to contain Memphis from the perimeter and committed 16 turnovers that led to 30 Grizzlies points. They made a push in the third quarter and cut a 23-point deficit to eight, but couldn't get the stops necessary to make it a game.

"I think we cut it to seven at some point and you should have been in the game, but we are not mature enough… we played against a team that played in a second of a back-to-back with the same travel that we had, and they played the right way, played really hard and we're not there yet. So, you know, go back and work and find ways to get better, because when you're not consistent and you don't find those ways, it's just like that's not what we want to do here," Fernandez said after the game.

The Nets briefly led 7-5, but Memphis responded with a 9-0 run and never let up control. Cedric Coward, Cam Spencer and Jaylen Wells got hot early, and a Wells' three-pointer forced a Brooklyn timeout with 7:55 remaining in the first quarter, with the Grizzlies flipping the score to 16-9 in their own favor.

The shooting didn't slow down. Memphis made nine three-pointers in the opening quarter and carried a 38-23 lead into the second. Brooklyn faced a 19-point deficit in the first half before making a small dent in it. The Grizzlies still led 71-54 at halftime.

"Right now the two practices we've had, we've practiced very well. So we practice better than we play, which is not a terrible sign. It's a frustrating sign because you believe you're better, but all we can do is go back to work."

Julius Randle said Brooklyn didn't match Memphis' urgency from the opening tip. The three-time All-Star pointed to the team's overall start as a bigger issue.

"We didn't punch first. We didn't come out with a sense of urgency, and they took advantage of that," he said.

"Just organization. I think maybe just trying too hard, playing a little unorganized, stuff like that," Randle said. "And then just attention to detail, you know, just think we got a lapse of focus sometimes."

Sparked by scoring from Noah Clowney, Day'Ron Sharpe, and Julius Randle, Brooklyn put together a strong third-quarter surge to cut the deficit to 85-77 with 5:12 remaining. Memphis took a 103-84 lead into the fourth quarter and eventually stretched the margin beyond 20.

It was Brooklyn's fifth loss by double figures.

"They got to grow fast," Fernandez said about the young group. "You know, like being 20 is not an excuse.…. I'm frustrated or I get mad because I know they're very good and they're better than this. And when I just don't see a connected group is, it hurts…"

Michael Porter Jr. attended Saturday's game after missing time for personal reasons. Fernández was asked about Porter's absence and whether he knew when the forward might return, but the coach declined.

Mikel Brown Jr. returned after missing the last two games. It's been a bit of a strange start and the guard missed the last two games for two different reasons — one for injury management and the other for an illness. The rookie finished with six points and two assists on 2-of-5 shooting in 20 minutes.

After the game, his father pointed out the importance of the floor general. Take it for whatever it's worth.

Brooklyn's trip to Memphis didn't go according to plan. The Nets were caught in Friday night's FAA ground stop after boarding their charter flight out of New Orleans, forcing the team to stay overnight before finally flying out Saturday morning.

The team arrived in Memphis around 11 a.m., just hours before its game against the Grizzlies. The unexpected delay also forced Brooklyn to scrap its planned morning shootaround.

"Yeah, I mean, obviously it was something that we couldn't control," head coach Jordi Fernández said. "And to be honest with you, it was not that bad. We had good rest and got here [Saturday] morning and did our walkthrough, and probably [would have] gone to the gym, but we were not able to. And I think we feel good and ready to go."

Fernández acknowledged that the altered schedule wasn't ideal, particularly for players who had grown accustomed to the team's usual pregame routine.

"Everybody's safe. It's the most important thing," he said.

The Nets are back home against the 76ers on Monday, November 16.

#2593. Game Preview: San Antonio Spurs at Utah Jazz

The Utah Jazz have responded to the hype they got in the off season by winning one of their first 13 games. Injuries to their two best players have a lot to do with that, but they've been playing predictably and are struggling to make outside shots. Being small with four perimeter players and a big with no offensive bag has made it harder to bend opposing defenses, as a result, ensuring that they stay in a transition game more than they like.

Still, it would be unwise to think they will roll over quickly. Flawed as they are, they can creep back in through the door if the San Antonio Spurs are playing with their food. Even if a team has a basement record, sometimes they show up stronger than the numbers because they are desperate to get back in the win column.

The Spurs will head into Delta Center on an 11-game win streak, tied for their sixth-longest in franchise history. The streak is long enough that every team in the NBA is well aware, adding a higher level of intrigue to the game. This will be the third matchup between these teams this season.

Spurs Injuries: Tobias Harris — out (left calf strain); Jayden Quaintance — out (right knee surgery); Maliq Brown — out (G League); Ja'Kobi Gillespie — out (G League)

#2591. Will Commanders try to put the Ben Sinnott genie back in the bottle? - Daily Slop

Editor's note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy!

Through Week 6, opponents had scored touchdowns on 18 of 22 red-zone trips against Washington, yet New York left crucial points behind when Frankie Luvu punched the ball loose from Malik Nabers at the 16-yard line and Jeremy Reaves recovered.

Washington also held the Giants to 4-of-12 on third down, including two critical late stops when it couldn't afford to give New York another first down—a defensive standard that will be tested immediately when Joe Burrow and the Bengals visit Landover.

One of the biggest turnarounds from the Commanders tie back in Week 5 against the Giants and their win over the Giants on Thursday night was the plan of attack against Cover-0. In Week 5, the Giants spammed Cover-0 blitzes throughout the second half and overtime and the Commanders just couldn't handle it. They continually attempted to take shots down the field to try and hit explosive plays rather than just finding a simple quick solution.

Daniels was seeing those blitzes a lot better and it showed in the most critical moment.

Having thrown two late interceptions, it looked like the Commanders season was over, but the defense bailed Daniels out and gave him another opportunity, which he wasn't going to pass up. On third and four with under a minute remaining in the game, the Giants of course show Daniels another Cover-0 blitz. This time, Daniels doesn't adjust the protection, but instead signals to Stefon Diggs in the slot to change his route. In the first game, when Daniels saw Cover-0, he often checked into a shot play to try and attack the blitz and throw a big touchdown over the top of it. But clearly this time they were looking to play smarter, and it worked out much better for them.

Daniels adjusts Diggs route, having him run a slant against the slot corner. When he snaps the ball, the defense comes on the blitz, but the defensive tackle to the right side of the line pops up and drops out into coverage, trying to take away a hot throw over the middle. Daniels just checked into a hot throw over the middle with Diggs running a slant, so that could potentially be a problem. But Daniels does a great job adjusting his throw to beat that defensive lineman dropping into coverage.

Diggs runs a great route, beating the corner with a nice stutter move before sharply cutting across his face to get inside. The throw from Daniels has to be slightly behind him because of that defensive lineman dropping into coverage, but Diggs does well to adjust to the pass and make the grab. Diggs breaks a diving tackle from the slot corner and gets some help from fellow receiver Van Jefferson, who helps block the other nearby defender. With both defenders out of the picture, Diggs runs uncontested into the end zone for a 32-yard game-winning touchdown.

It goes to show that you can still score a big touchdown against Cover-0 without having to try and take a deep shot constantly. As I said back in Week 5, I don't mind that their philosophy against Cover-0 is to go on the attack, in fact I quite like it. It offers you one-on-one matchups and I like that they feel like they can take shots with those matchups. But they clearly went too far in Week 5 in trying to throw bombs down the field. This game proved there's more ways to go about it. Winning a one-on-one doesn't have to be 20 yards down the field, it can be a quick slant like this when you have Stefon Diggs or Antonio Williams in the slot. With it being Cover-0, if you win that one-on-one quickly, there's every chance the receiver can run freely after the catch and score as there's no safety help over the top.

So credit should go to David Blough and Jayden Daniels for making that adjustment. It's a shame they couldn't have made it back in Week 5 because they would have won that game too if they had, but it paid off for them this time around and it meant that the Commanders have just about kept their season alive.

After catching just 17 passes over his first two-plus NFL seasons behind Zach Ertz and Chig Okonkwo, third-year tight end Ben Sinnott stepped in when Okonkwo exited Thursday night's game with a back injury and delivered four receptions for 42 yards and a touchdown.

Sinnott hurdled a defender to convert a critical first down on the final drive of the first half before hauling in a go-ahead score on third-and-goal, then added a 24-yard catch-and-run early in the third quarter. He has now caught 21 of 24 career targets, making a strong case for offensive coordinator David Blough to feature more two-tight-end sets down the stretch.

In two-tight-end packages, Commanders offensive coordinator David Blough should give Sinnott a few defined passing-game opportunities on early downs and near the goal line. Blough should continue his approach of giving each tight end their own distinct role, but should also look to take advantage of Sinnott's receiving and after-the-catch ability that, until Thursday night, was going to waste.

If Okonkwo is back to his usual workload against Cincinnati, I'll be watching the snaps he shares with Sinnott. When Washington needs a first down and both tight ends are out there, does Daniels go back to Sinnott?

Brandon Aiyuk has made no secret of where he wants to resume his career, regularly appearing in Commanders gear on Instagram as he works back from his 2024 knee injury. Daniels completed 23 of 33 attempts for 249 yards and a season-high three touchdown passes. According to Next Gen Stats, all three touchdown passes came against Cover 0, a blitz-heavy design New York used successfully and often during the 27-27 Week 5 tie.

The three scores were also on passes between the numbers, a feat Daniels previously achieved once in 2024, during a Week 17 win over the Falcons. That accomplishment flies in the face of pre-draft criticism regarding a supposed allergy to throwing over the middle. Ironically, both interceptions were on throws outside the numbers.

Wherever the ball needed to go, the quarterback wasn't about to let the Commanders' season spiral further south. "I didn't want to let my team down in that moment," Daniels said, "so when they gave me another opportunity to go out there and win the game, I didn't want to let them down."

The scary part for defenses is that Daniels is starting to find a rhythm after five consecutive starts.

I'm tired of watching the Eagles change offensive coordinators every year or two, only to end up dealing with the same problems.

Bad protection, predictable plays, poor adjustments, and talented players not living up to their potential.

At what point do we stop blaming execution and start looking at the people responsible for teaching these players?

Prediction: 49ers 27, Cowboys 17 — Jon Machota, Cowboys beat writer

Turns out, all six of Zvada's misses this season — three pushed wide right and three yanked wide left — have come from the right hash.

It is fair to say that Zvada's struggles were critical parts of why the Giants tied and lost games to the Commanders, rather than winning both games. He missed three kicks in the tie to Washington in Week 5, and his miss Thursday came in a 3-point loss.

The point here isn't to debate which decisions Harbaugh made correctly, and which he didn't. Though discussing that is certainly fair game. The point is that Zvada's continued misses are complicating the decision-making and costing the Giants points that are probably costing them games.

In an NFC East race that seems likely to go down to the wire, and where every decision, every made or missed kick, everything that happens in the margins of an NFL game, could end up making the difference how much rope can the Giants give Zvada to figure it out?

Aaryavir Sehwag has spoken about the nerves he felt during India's 2026 Under-19 Asia Cup final against Pakistan, revealing that he kept chanting 'Sita Ram, Sita Ram' to calm himself down. The young batter shared the moment during a video call with his father, former India cricketer Virender Sehwag, who posted their conversation on social media after India's title win."Papa, I was so nervous… was just chanting Sita Ram, Sita Ram!" Aaryavir told his father while recalling the tense moments of the final.Sharing the video, Virender said such moments meant more to him than awards and trophies."From winning Player of the Tournament to recalling those nail-biting final moments, a very special conversation with beta Aaryavir. Some moments are bigger than awards, runs and trophies. These are the memories a father will cherish forever. May you always keep your feet firmly on the ground and touch the skies with your hardwork and talent," he wrote.Aaryavir scored 58 off 61 balls in India's chase of 338 against Pakistan in the final in Oman on Saturday. India secured the title with a last-ball four from Mohit Ulva. Aaryavir was named Player of the Tournament after scoring 361 runs in five matches at an average of 90.25 and a strike rate of over 95. His tally included one century and three half-centuries. He also hit 16 sixes, the most in the tournament, and scored half-centuries in both the semi-final and final.In the video shared by Virender, Aaryavir also recalled the final over, when India needed eight runs with one wicket remaining. He said chanting 'Sitaram' helped him deal with the pressure. He also told his father that Pakistani supporters had chanted 'Sehwag' 'Sehwag' while he was batting. Virender is known for his performances in Pakistan, including scoring India's first Test triple century in Multan.

Pakistan, who were asked to bat first, posted 337/9. Usman Khan top-scored with 107 off 111 balls, hitting 11 fours and three sixes. After his dismissal, Mohit remained unbeaten on 49 off 26 balls, hitting five fours and three sixes, while Chigurupati Venkata contributed an unbeaten 11 to help India complete the chase.

If he scores 20 goals this season, he'll tie Gordie Howe for the most 20-goal campaigns at 22.

#2587. Kyrie Irving reflects on 2016 championship in return to Cleveland: ‘I’m so grateful for all the Cavs fans’

CLEVELAND — Robert Frost said, "Home is the place where, when you have to go there, they have to take you in."

There was a time when Cleveland Cavaliers fans weren't eager to take Kyrie Irving in. His trade demands in the summer of 2017 derailed the franchise's best era of basketball. But time heals all wounds. Irving will always have a home in Cleveland — that's what delivering a championship ensures you.

"You know, 52 years is a long, long period of time waiting for a championship, and we did it," Irving said after Dallas Mavericks 127-117 loss to Cleveland on Saturday. "And I think that's one of the hardest championships — I think. I'm not gonna say it is, I said I think personally it's one of the hardest championships ever in NBA history that we got to accomplish."

It's also a championship the city is still celebrating. On Saturday, the Cavs recognized the 10th anniversary of the 2016 championship by bringing out former general manager David Griffin to pull out the sword at the start of the game. They also played a video tribute commemorating Irving's championship-clinching shot in Game 7, which brought the crowd to its feet.

"This one felt a lot different than the other times," Irving said of the reception. "This time I got to really settle in, really ground myself, and embrace the support that's here for me."

Irving's time in Cleveland was far from straightforward — he detailed how when asked about it on Saturday.

His rookie season came during the lockout that lasted until December. This meant that he couldn't communicate with anyone on the coaching staff or front office. "So my first entry into here was a little awkward."

Things didn't get easier after that. The criticism he received when the Cavs initially fell short of expectations is something he still carries.

"When they're discussing my career," Irving said, "everybody likes to gear towards my first three years in the league, and like to put, 'He's not a winner. He didn't win anything. He didn't do anything without Bron (LeBron James). He didn't do anything without the players we ended up winning a championship with,' which I think is all a good and fair criticism, but I think as I look at it, it was just me learning."

The idea that a 21-year-old guard could single-handedly turn around a team that frankly wasn't very talented was unreasonable at the time, and looks even more absurd in retrospect.

James's return in 2014 didn't lighten the burden. The expectations, externally and internally, only grew. Irving admitted that this led to tough conversations with his teammates. "You don't go home happy all the time even when you're winning, because you feel like you can still continue to get better."

"What I remember most is that championship was so tough."

The championship season was a difficult one for Irving. He fractured his kneecap during Game 1 of the 2015 Finals, which kept him out until December of the following season. And when he did come back, he thought he wasn't playing to his standards. "It felt like there was a lot of pressure on me to perform well."

This was a theme for him and that team throughout a turbulent 2016 season that saw them switch coaches from David Blatt to Ty Lue halfway through.

"It's all on me at times, or it's all on Bron, or it's all on somebody else, K Love," Irving said. "It's like the blame game got split between us three, but it usually came between Bron and me. It just prepared me. You gotta be an MFer in this league. You gotta have short-term memory."

Those difficult times paid off in the championship. The 3-1 comeback was made possible by three of the best individual performances by him and James — culminating in Irving's shot to decide Game 7.

"When I look at it now, I'm just grateful that I was playing against the best of the best, going against the best teams in the world, getting everybody's best shot for about three straight years," Irving said. "A lot of young players never get to experience that, being on the hunt for championships every single year. I take those little moments and try my best to connect it to the fans here, because we couldn't have done it without them."

It's been a decade since the championship and nine years since Irving last wore a Cavs jersey, yet, the bond between the player and city may be stronger now than ever. Saturday's reception, and what it meant to Irving, is proof of that.

"It's been 10 years. It's been a great reflection point for me to be able to come back and be able to receive that support in a different way," Irving said. "I'm so grateful for all the Cavs fans, Cleveland in general, Ohio, wrapping their arms around me as well, and also sticking it through with me as I was a young person."

There were only a handful of people waiting for Irving after he filed out of the Mavs media interview room an hour and a half after the game ended. One of them politely thanked Irving for 2016 and all that it meant to them.

Irving graciously looked down at them with a wide smile and said, "We're champions forever."

#2586. Rangers lose star goaltender Igor Shesterkin for season with lower-body injury; what's next for New York?

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

New York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin will miss the remainder of the season with a lower-body injury, the team announced on Saturday.

Shesterkin suffered an apparent leg injury in the Rangers' loss to the Washington Capitals on Friday night as his right leg slid awkwardly into the post while scrambling to get back in position. Shesterkin fell to the ice immediately, and he needed assistance to get down the tunnel.

Prior to that loss, the Rangers were off to a terrific 4-1-0 start, and Shesterkin was a driving force behind that success. In just five appearances, Shesterkin posted 3.90 goals saved above average with a .900 high-danger save percentage, according to Natural Stat Trick.

The 2022 Vezina Trophy winner, Shesterkin has put up sparkling numbers since he entered the NHL in 2019-20. In 330 games, Shesterkin boasts a .917 save percentage, a 2.51 GAA and 22 shutouts. Over the last three full seasons from 2023-26, Shesterkin ranked third in goals saved above average with 45.4. Only Connor Hellebuyck and Andrei Vasilevskiy were better in that category.

Shesterkin was a big reason why the Rangers felt they could bounce back from a disappointing 2025-26 season, and losing the star goaltender puts a huge dent in the team's playoff hopes. It doesn't help that backup goalie Joonas Korpisalo is also hurt.

Dylan Garand replaced Shesterkin on Friday night, and Spencer Martin will be recalled from the AHL after recovering from his own injury. With the Rangers playing well early, it wouldn't be a shock to see them explore better replacement options for Shesterkin.

New York won't be able to replace Shesterkin's impact because he's one of the five best goalies in the world. However, the team should be able to upgrade its current goaltending situation, which is a fairly low bar to clear.

First, there are unsigned veterans still on the open market in Petr Mrazek and James Reimer. Neither one was great last season -- hence their availability at the moment -- Reimer and Mrazek could provide a level of stability in the crease that the Rangers simply don't have right now.

New York could also explore trade possibilities, and Minnesota Wild netminder Filip Gustavsson could be a solution there. Jesper Wallstedt is the future of the crease in Minnesota, making Gustavsson more of a luxury. Would the Wild send Gustavsson to New York in exchange for some draft capital it could use to acquire a center?

The one snag in a potential Gustavsson deal is his contract. Gustavsson is in the first year of a deal that pays him $6.8 million over the next five seasons. That's a big commitment for a player who will become a backup when Shesterkin returns.

Obviously, Connor Hellebuyck has been on the trade market for months now, but that trade wouldn't make sense for the Rangers. Hellebuyck is on an expensive long-term deal, and New York would have $20 million tied up in goalies if they made that move, not to mention the astronomical acquisition cost.

However, if you'll allow me to get creative here, it's no secret that the Florida Panthers have pursed Hellebuyck. What if the Panthers traded Jacob Markstrom -- just acquired in the offseason -- to the Rangers in order to make room for Hellebuyck?

Markstrom does have a 20-team no-trade list, so the question is whether New York would be one of his 11 approved teams. Florida flipping Markstrom so quickly seems like a long shot, but the team has taken plenty of big swings in recent history.

#2583. Big Ten power rankings after Week 11: USC moves down after loss

The race for a spot in the Big Ten Championship, and subsequently the College Football Playoff, is heating up, and we're seeing some monumental matchups across the league as we get deep into November.

It was the USC Trojans and Indiana Hoosiers who had the headline matchup on Saturday, with Curt Cignetti sending Lincoln Riley packing, a result that led to the Trojans sliding in our power rankings once again. We also saw Dan Lanning's Oregon Ducks pick up another big win, this time over the Michigan Wolverines, while the Ohio State Buckeyes outlast the Northwestern Wildcats, and the Maryland Terrapins got a big upset win over the Wisconsin Badgers.

With two weeks of regular-season play remaining, the next couple of weeks will be fascinating as teams jockey for position and try to grab the two spots in the Big Ten championship game.

Here are our Big Ten Power Rankings after Week 8:

Analysis: Every time it seems like Rutgers has hit rock bottom, they find a way to dig deeper. Another blowout loss isn't a shock, but the fact that Rutgers came out and announced that Greg Schiano would be sticking around for next season was a surprise. I'm not sure what else the Scarlet Knights are hoping to see from him, but the misery is continuing in Piscataway.

Analysis: This Purdue is a far cry from the September firepower we saw earlier this season. Ryan Browne was ineffective all night, and there was no light in the defense either. It's been a strange season for the Boilermakers, and it's tough to see another win on the schedule.

Analysis: Maryland, even with a backup quarterback, has some momentum suddenly. It's too little, too late, of course, but Cardell Williams did enough to help the Terrapins pull off a surprising win at home, and the pass rush closed out the game. There are some pieces on the roster that are revealing themselves as must-keep players for whoever takes over as head coach. Looking at you, Brian Kelly.

Analysis: Michigan State's defense seems to be finding some things that are working, but the uncertainty at quarterback and injuries to key playmakers on offense make the Spartans very similar to their in-state counterparts, Michigan. Things need to break right for the offense to have success, and much of that is reliant on the defense forcing turnovers. There was some momentum in the first half, but the Huskies clamped down in the second half and didn't provide many opportunities. The Spartans' depth is running thin at several positions.

Analysis: Minnesota has played up or down to its competition for most of the season. Given the disappointing season Penn State has had, the Golden Gophers appeared ready to match a dud performance, but they once again got stomped at the line of scrimmage and let the Nittany Lions toy with them on the ground. The rollercoaster season for PJ Fleck continues.

Analysis: Talk about a dejected team. Michigan only showed some energy after a long drive to end the third quarter, danced during "Shout!" and was then turned away at the goal line. The experiment of playing both Tommy Carr and Bryce Underwood was odd, as they swapped out without much rhyme or reason, and although the Wolverines rushed for 200 yards, 70 of it came on one play. The vaunted defense was finally tested downfield, and it broke. Kyle Whittingham's seat was already warm, and the eject button might be getting pushed soon.

Analysis: Wisconsin couldn't contain a backup quarterback that was thrust into action at the last minute. That speaks to the peaks and valleys of this season for the Badgers. Maryland has been without direction for months, and yet when it needed to the most, Maryland was able to throw on the Badgers' defense and get a late stop. Ryan Hopkins and Colton Joseph are clearly not up to the task of leading the offense, and there isn't enough talent up front to support a run game. It looked like a high school product at times, and the season has officially gone off the rails in Madison.

Analysis: For the first time in a month, Nebraska ran the ball well with both Jamal Rule and Anthony Colandrea, which opened up some of the intermediate passing opportunities for the veteran quarterback. The Cornhuskers' offense got a boost from the coordinator change, but facing the Rutgers defense is also a good cure for offensive woes. It was a step in the right direction, but Nebraska has much bigger fish to fry moving forward with Ohio State and Iowa left on the schedule.

Week 11 Result: 21-14 Win vs. Michigan State

Analysis: Washington tried to give the game away with a muffed punt in the fourth quarter, but the defense did stand tall in the second half and forced the Spartans to put together long drives if they wanted to win. Demond Williams did damage in the first half, but much of his yardage came on the final drive of the game that led to the winning touchdown, and the Huskies were otherwise quiet. Inconsistency on offense has plagued Washington all season, and it was on display on Saturday. The Huskies did earn bowl eligibility at the right time, with both Indiana and Oregon left on the schedule.

Analysis: Looking at the final score and watching how Katin Houser played, it's pretty remarkable that the Illini had a chance to win. Houser tossed three picks and should have had even more, but the rainy conditions probably helped him out a little bit. The offensive line was no match for UCLA's blitz packages, and the early big plays the Bruins hit were never answered. Illinois has a tough finish to the season coming up with Iowa and Northwestern left.

Analysis: Penn State continued to establish its identity on the ground with big days from Carson Hansen and Cam Wallace. The defense sacked Drake Lindsey three times and forced incompletions with pressure. Rocco Becht played through injury and capitalized when he did get to throw the ball, which wasn't often. It might have taken nearly a full season, but the Nittany Lions now know how this team can win offensively, and they could rise to eight wins to finish the regular season with just Rutgers and Maryland left on the schedule.

Analysis: Missing Aidan Chiles has really hurt Northwestern the past two weeks. The offense as a whole hasn't changed much, but his playmaking and ability to open rushing lanes have completely changed the unit's effectiveness. Northwestern doesn't have the athletes defensively to go toe-to-toe with Ohio State, and although a late score dressed up the final score, the Wildcats were playing catch-up throughout. Northwestern does have two winnable games to end the season, but Chiles' health is the biggest factor moving forward.

Week 11 Result: 28-19 Win vs. Northwestern

Analysis: The Buckeyes decided to throw it to Jeremiah Smith this week, and to nobody's surprise, that was a winning formula. He set more records and topped 100 yards with a touchdown again, and Ohio State cruised to a win. The Buckeyes picked up five sacks and flustered the Northwestern offense for much of the day and were always in control, even if the scoreboard looked somewhat close.

Analysis: USC's playoff dreams are likely finished with another loss on the road in a big game. Jayden Maiava played one of his worst games, tossing three interceptions. The Trojans got down inside the 30-yard line six times, but only managed 13 points thanks to turnovers and missed field goals. The Lincoln Riley question continues to loom large, but it will be interesting to see how hard the team plays in the final two games.

Analysis: It's still odd to think that Iowa has a couple of star pass-catchers, but Braeden Jackson is a difference-maker on offense and special teams, and Tony Diaz is the gadget man that the Hawkeyes are always trying to get the ball to. Jackson and Diaz both scored against Purdue and helped Hank Brown remain efficient on a big day for the offense. The Hawkeyes know how to control the clock and should be able to run the ball to victory in their final two games, but they have a reliable passing attack, finally. Iowa does need some help to get to the conference championship game.

Analysis: Oregon is playing to its potential right now, even without Dante Moore. Dylan Raiola is playing the best ball of his life, Dakorien Moore is breaking into superstar territory, and the defense is playing complementary football. The Ducks weren't afraid to test a talented Michigan defense vertically, and they let their athletes win. Oregon has a short turnaround this week heading on the road to Michigan State, but it's very reasonable to see the Ducks winning out and potentially backing into an at-large bid for the playoff.

Analysis: Hello, Grant Wilson. The Hoosiers didn't need Josh Hoover, as Wilson got the start and threw for 305 yards and two touchdowns, and he had time to operate thanks to a potent rushing attack in front of him. Indiana does have something of a quarterback conundrum on its hands whenever Hoover gets healthy. The Indiana defense is the story, however, applying pressure throughout and making USC's offense collapse in on itself. Indiana has the indie track to the Big Ten title game, with a trip to Washington and a home date against Purdue remaining.

Analysis: UCLA ground out another win with Ty Dieffenbach, although it once again was not pretty. Dieffenbach played through injury after briefly leaving the game before halftime. Most of his damage came in the first half, and Aidan Mizell has emerged as his favorite target downfield. As a result of the reliance on the big passing plays, the run game, which was the Bruins' calling card to start the season, has struggled to be as consistent. The tailbacks averaged just 3.2 yards per carry. The Bruins will be tested in the trenches the next two weeks at Michigan and at home against USC.

With the regular season winding down, the focus is beginning to shift to the Big Ten championship game, which will be the final conference title game played by the Big Ten before college football moves to a 24-team playoff next season. Here are the updated Big Ten football standings following the results of Week 11.

UCLA will go into Week 12 as the first team in the Big Ten in position to clinch a spot in this year's Big Ten football championship game in Indianapolis. The Bruins remain undefeated in Big Ten play and have the luxury of having room for error in the final two weeks. All UCLA needs is one win in its final two games against Michigan and USC to secure one of the two spots in the Big Ten title game.

Defending Big Ten champion Indiana is the next team in line but will still have to win out to guarantee a spot in the Big Ten title game for a second consecutive season. In the fourth quarter of a Week 9 game the Cowboys led by only three points, Dallas forced — and recovered — a fumble by Colts running back Jonathan Taylor. The ensuing celebration drew a penalty.

Said referee Clay Martin in announcing the specific of theinfraction, "Unsportsmanlike conduct by Dallas, who had a non-uniformed player in the blue sweats and a stocking cap come onto the field to celebrate."

The non-uniformed player in the blue sweats and the stocking cap was linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, who was inactive for the game due to injury.

While violations of the celebration rules routinely spark fines, Overshown was not financially penalized by the league.

It's possible Overshown got some sort of punishment from the team, especially since owner and G.M. Jerry Jones rejected Overshown's claim that he didn't know it was against the rules for a player not in uniform to run onto the field for a celebration.

"I don't think that," Jones said. "I really don't. I think that he's been involved in football at Texas, and he's been involved here, and he knows that, at every level, a nonparticipant can't run out on the field."

Every player should have known the rule before last Sunday. Given what happened in the Dallas game, where the lost 15 yards of field position set the stage for a game-tying field goal by the Colts (the Cowboys eventually won, 27-23), there's even less of an excuse to not know it now.

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here.

One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.

That made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh.

As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.

When it comes to how the talent broke down by conference, it was a a pretty level playing field for the most part.

Not to spoil anyting, but Arizona freshman Caleb Holt did not make the cut. He did, however, turn some heads in the Wildcats' exhibition game.

Loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.

It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.

Our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko. After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal.

Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.

Look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.

Steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?

Finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an issue is Missouri QB Austin Simmons. After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

#2571. Rüdiger set for emotional Germany farewell in Berlin

After making 86 appearances for Germany, Antonio Rüdiger announced his international retirement at the beginning of September.

“After taking some time to reflect, I feel the time has come for me to end my career with the national team and make way for the younger generation,” Rüdiger said in a statement back then.

It has now been announced that the Real Madrid defender will receive an official farewell from the German Football Association (DFB) ahead of Monday's UEFA Nations League clash with the Netherlands at the Olympiastadion in his hometown of Berlin.

The tribute will mark the end of a 12-year international career for the 33-year-old, who made his Germany debut in May 2014.

Rüdiger has made seven appearances for Real Madrid this season and remains under contract with the Spanish giants until 2027.

#2563. Connor Hellebuyck trade: Jets send star goalie to the Devils in exchange for four players, two draft picks

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil. The star goalie for the Winnipeg Jets is on the move after being traded to New Jersey on Friday in exchange for four players and two future draft picks. the teams announced the move with the Jets receiving Dawson Mercer, Nick Bjugstad, Nico Daws and Alexander Command, plus a 2027 seventh-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.

Hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August. He said at the time that he had made the request months earlier and tried to keep the situation private.

Hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No. 130 overall. He's recognized as one of the best goalies in the league as a three-time Vezina Trophy winner. He also helped carry the United States to its first gold medal since 1980 at the 2026 Olympics in February with some incredible saves against Canada in the final game.

After trading Jacob Markstom in the offseason, the Devils had a clear need in goal, and this splashy move certainly fills that need. With a talented young core already in place, New Jersey's Stanley Cup window is wide open.

RAISE HELLE!Connor Hellebuyck is a New Jersey Devil: https://t.co/HCehRGOQI5 pic.twitter.com/dZGNQR16m1

For the Jets, it must be a hard pill to swallow when a franchise icon decides to walk out they door, but this trade package should help them as the enter a new era and revamp the roster. Winnipeg got a former first-rounder in Mercer to try and add to a rebuild as well as a veteran presence in Bjugstad. They also acquired a younger goalie in Daws who could fill the role of Hellebuyck at just 25 years old.

Goaltending has been an issue in New Jersey for a while now -- even after the team acquired Markstrom from the Calgary Flames in 2024. Markstom never really panned out, and his 13.6 goals allowed above average, per Natural Stat Trick, were a big reason why the Devils missed the postseason last year.

In the early portion of this season, it was clear that New Jersey needed to make a move to upgrade in the crease. Daws and veteran Jake Allen simply aren't a tandem suitable for a Stanley Cup contender, and the numbers backed that up. New Jersey ranks 24th in team save percentage at .877, and the duo of Daws and Allen combined to surrender 2.99 goals above average.

Once Hellebuyck gets up to game speed, that shouldn't be a problem anymore.

In the three-season stretch from 2023-26, Hellebuyck led the NHL with 73.42 goals saved above average, which is 20 goals higher than the next closest netminder. Over that span, Hellebuyck also posted a standard save percentage of .914 and an astronomical high-danger save-percentage of .832.

Hellebuyck carried less talented teams to the playoffs multiple times in his career. Now on a team loaded with weaponry in their prime -- Jack Hughes, Jesper Bratt and Nico Hischier to name a few -- Hellebuyck could be the final piece to the championship puzzle.

In terms of the acquisition cost, it was probably an easy deal for Devils general manager Sunny Mehta to make. The 2029 second-round pick is useless for a team that should be all-in now, Bjugstad is simply a depth piece and Daws now has no path to a starting role with Hellebuyck in town.

The most interesting trade chips are Mercer and Command. Mercer flashed major upside with 56 points in his second NHL season, 2022-23, but he hasn't really come close to hitting those heights again. Still, even if he has plateaued, Mercer remains a strong middle-six forward rising into his prime.

Although Command had his detractors -- and may have been over-drafted at No. 12 overall -- he was a consensus first-round pick last summer. That gives Winnipeg a potential franchise forward it can build around long-term, but New Jersey already has one of the deepest forward groups in the league, especially with the emergence of Arseny Gritsyuk and the acquisition of Luke Evangelista.

If we're looking for a 3-D chess angle of this deal, it only makes the Devils more appealing for a certain Minnesota Wild defenseman whose brothers just happen to play in New Jersey already. Grade -- A+

Let's get the obvious out of the way first: The Jets were never going to get fair value for Hellebuyck because, at his best, he's the No. 1 goaltender in the world with no equal. That type of excellence can't be replaced.

That said, Winnipeg did fairly well given the circumstances. Hellebuyck made a public trade request, and he wasn't even with the team after sitting out for the entirety of training camp. The entire league knew the Jets had to trade him.

Hellebuyck's talent created a decent market anyway, but most of the suitors were bona fide Stanley Cup contenders with little in the way of valuable draft capital, and they weren't going to knee cap the roster by sending a key player back in return.

With all that taken into consideration, Kevin Cheveldayoff got a solid return. Although Mercer's ceiling may be lower than initially thought, he's a 24-year-old forward who banks roughly 20 goals and 20 assists every season. The kicker with Mercer will be Winnipeg's ability to re-sign him before he hits restricted free agency next summer.

The addition of Command means Winnipeg now has two forwards selected in the top 12 of the 2026 NHL Draft after taking center Viggo Bjorck themselves. If both of those players deliver on their first-round pedigrees, they could be a terrific one-two punch for the team long-term.

Daws was a third-round pick in 2020, and despite playing just 13 NHL games since the start of the 2024-25 season, he should give Winnipeg a solid back up option behind Stuart Skinner. It certainly helps that Skinner is off to a great start with his new team -- and if Daws develops into a true No. 1 -- it'll be gravy.

If there's any reason to critique this deal from the Jets' side of things, it's that they didn't get premium draft capital or a surefire up-and-coming prospect. Maybe Command develops into a star, but there's no guarantee he becomes a top-six stud in the NHL.

The Jets got a lot of good stuff, but they didn't really get anything great, at least not based on what we know in the moment. Because of that, I have to ding Winnipeg a little bit. Grade: B

#2561. Dortmund confirm controversial sponsorship deal with Rheinmetall will not be renewed

Borussia Dortmund have confirmed that their controversial sponsorship deal with arms manufacturer Rheinmetall – which expires on 30 June, 2027 – will not be renewed.

The partnership, which began in 2024, had sparked heated debates over the past two years. Among other things, a members' vote was held which demonstrated strong opposition.

From the results in 2024, a majority of 855 of the 1,205 members present [currently a total of approximately 245,000] voted against the Rheinmetall deal.

Their argument for voting against it was arms manufacturer, among other things, how it earns its money from war, not peace – values that, in their view, are incompatible with Dortmund.

As BILD writes, the decision by BVB's chiefs to part ways with their lucrative Rheinmetall deal when the contract expires in June 2027 is likely to have a positive impact on the atmosphere ahead of the upcoming general meeting.

Carsten Cramer, Chairman of Borussia Dortmund, released a statement via the club's website regarding their decision to terminate the collaboration and reject an extension beyond June 2027:

“First of all, I would like to emphasize that we did not make this decision alone, but together with Rheinmetall,” Cramer explained in the aforementioned statement.

"We are, of course, aware that our partnership has been the subject of controversial discussion since its inception. We are aware of the criticism from our members and some of the fans.

At the 2024 general meeting, the members voted on a motion not to extend the partnership agreement with Rheinmetall beyond 2027. We naturally took this aspect into account and seriously in our discussions with Rheinmetall.

"The decision wasn't easy for me. But if we so clearly advocate for the 50+1 rule and the unity and cohesion of BVB are as important to you as they are to me.

“Then we have to consider all the perspectives and considerations of our stakeholders and ultimately make a decision,” Cramer concluded on the matter.

#2557. What Bill Belichick said after loss to Louisville

The North Carolina Tar Heels had the chance to become bowl-eligible by getting their sixth win on Saturday night against Louisville. While the Tar Heels hung around for all of the game, they weren't able to pull it out.

Louisville got a late score and then stopped to end any North Carolina comeback in Chapel Hill, beating the Tar Heels 16-14. The loss sends UNC to 5-5 on the year, and they have two games left to try and get that sixth win.

While UNC's defense was up to the task in this one, the offense struggled. The eventual departure of Billy Edwards saw freshman Travis Burgess take over and while he moved the ball down the field, he couldn't find a way to get that key score when they needed it.

After the game, head coach Bill Belichick met the media to discuss the tough loss for the Tar Heels. All quotes via Inside Carolina.

"We all saw it. I don't think I have too much to add, really. A hard-fought game came down to a handful of plays, and we just weren't able to make enough of them tonight. Louisville's a good team, good offense, hard to stop, but they still move the ball, and it's challenging. I thought Travis stepped in there, did a good job, and the opportunity that he got gave some spark, he made some plays. But in the end, we just couldn't get enough done."

"Just got everybody out of there as quickly as possible. Play the game between the whistles, and that's not what we're here for."

"We were down by six. We weren't down there very much today, so we got down there, I thought that was an opportunity for us to score."

"I haven't gone back into my office. I haven't seen anything. I'm standing on the sideline. I didn't see what happened. Guys out there, we got out there and got everybody off as quickly as possible."

"Thought he came in there in a tough situation, made some plays, made a couple of plays with his legs on a scramble. Made a couple of good throws. Took us down for a touchdown."

"Billy's taken a lot more plays than Travis has, so there were things that Travis just hasn't had enough opportunity to do yet. So we did the things that he felt comfortable with."

"We were in long yardage on three straight drives. Sacked on a screen pass. We got a penalty. Had another negative play, and so, too many long-yardage plays on first down."

"Every game has its own dynamic, so they made a couple more plays than we did. We make progress every week, so do the teams we're playing."

"It's probably developed during the season."

This article originally appeared on Tar Heels Wire: What Bill Belichick said after loss to Louisville

#2555. Group of retired MLB umpires, including Joe West, file lawsuit alleging they are owed more than $2 million

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Former MLB umpire Joe West is part of a group of five retired umpires who are suing their pension plan and alleging they have been underpaid by the plan, the Associated Press reports. West, along with Tom Hallion, Gerry Davis, Larry Vanover, and Jerry Layne, filed the suit in late September in federal court in New York.

The suit alleges that the five umpires have been underpaid by the pension plan by more than $2 million. According to the AP, the suit "was filed against the American Leagues and National Leagues of Professional Baseball Clubs Retirement Income Plan for Umpires and that entity's retirement committee." The five umpires claim their benefits were not calculated correctly and therefore should receive additional money.

West, 74, retired from umpiring in MLB in 2021 after umpiring more than 5,000 games at the highest level starting in 1976. The man they called "Cowboy Joe" umpired a record 5,460 games in all, was known as a colorful figure in the sport and sometimes even a source of controversy.

In 2021, West won more than $500,000 in damages as the result of a defamation suit against former MLB player Paul Lo Duca after Lo Duca alleged during a podcast that West would "open up the strike zone" for reliever Billy Wagner in exchange for driving one of Wagner's vintage cars.

West referenced his "history with lawsuits" on Thursday. From the AP:

West said that when he brought up the issue to the retirement committee, he was offered a relatively small sum. West said MLB senior vice president and chief employment counsel Steven Gonzalez told him: "If you don't like the number, sue us."

"Does Steve Gonzalez not know my history with dealing with lawsuits?" West said.

Like West, Davis also retired after the 2021 season while Hallion umpired through the 2022 season and Layne and Vanover stepped away after the 2024 campaign. The five sued as individuals and did not involve the umpires' union, their lawyer, Paul B. Holmes, said, per the AP.

A pretrial conference in the case is scheduled for Dec. 11.

#2554. Nikita Kucherov trade request: Five potential landing spots for the reigning NHL MVP

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

One of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey. According to Sportsnet, Nikita Kucherov has told the Lightning he won't sign a contract extension and has requested a trade.

Kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era. The 33-year-old just passed the legendary Steven Stamkos for the all-time franchise lead in points and has shown no signs of slowing down.

Just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win. His underlying numbers were even better with a five-on-five goal differential of plus-38 and an expected goals share of 57.0 percent. Only a select few players can drive play from the wing like Kucherov, and that makes him a unicorn of sorts.

Kucherov is in the final year of a contract that pays him $9.5 million per season, and with the salary cap rising rapidly, he's due for a gargantuan raise next summer. It sounds like Kucherov and the Lightning were too far apart on that number, so the superstar winger has shifted his focuse to a change of scenery.

It's important to note that Kucherov has limited trade protection in the form of a 10-team trade list, but that should be more than enough for the Lightning to find a suitable trade partner. With that in mind, let's take a look at five teams that would be ideal fits for Kucherov as he prepares for the next chapter of his illustrious career.

Right out of the gate, this is the most natural fit of all the potential landing spots. General manager Kent Hughes has done a superb job of locking down his young core on team-friendly contracts, and as a result, the Canadiens have nearly $30 million in projected cap space for next season. They also have a glaring need in their top two lines, and I'd say the reigning Hart Trophy winner would fill that role quite nicely.

Montreal's moment to strike is now. It's an ascendant team with a great salary cap situtation and assets to spend. It's time to make a splash, and this would be a tsunami. Just imagine Kucherov on a power play unit with Nick Suzuki, Cole Caufield, Lane Hutson and Ivan Demidov. Kucherov would also be coached by former Lightning teammate Martin St. Louis, so a rapport would already exist between player and coach. I expect the Canadiens to do everything in their power to land Kucherov.

We already know the Wild are big-game hunting at forward because they've been heavily linked to former Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin. If I were advising general manager Bill Guerin -- and I'm certainly not -- I would recommend Minnesota package whatever assets it has offered Detroit and redirect them to Tampa Bay. No, Kucherov is not a center,  and that's the Wild's biggest need.

However, Kucherov is a rare breed of winger in that he can drive play better than most first-line centers from the wing. Put him on a line with Kirill Kaprizov, and the only time opponents will touch the puck is when they're pulling out of the net.

With Quinn Hughes also on an expiring contract, acquiring Kucherov would be a risky move for the Wild. What if they give up premium assets only to lose Kucherov and Hughes next summer? I don't think fear can dictate Minnesota's decisions. The team has a top-two defenseman in the world on its roster right now, and it has the opportunity to acquire a top-five forward. Worry about next summer when the time comes. Go all in to win the Cup while you have a chance.

It was no secret that the Hurricanes were in on the Connor Hellebuyck sweepstakes but just missed out. So, if they can't get better at preventing goals, why not get much better at scoring them? Carolina doesn't exactly need any help offensively, but adding Kucherov would go a long way to helping the team repeat as Stanley Cup champions. Besides, Kucherov would provide another level of playmaking and finishing that the Canes don't currently have on their roster.

Carolina has a good chunk of cap space available already, and it wouldn't need to shed much in order to make room for Kucherov. The Canes also have some enticing young players on their roster that might appeal to the Bolts, and they have three first-round picks over the next two drafts. Why not take a shot at landing a superstar winger?

Similar to the Hurricanes, the Mammoth were in the mix to acquire Hellebucyk, and for good reason. The goaltending tandem of Karel Vejmelka and Sebastian Cossa has not been good, so Utah may have to outscore its problems until one of the goalies finds a groove. Offense may be the best defense for the Mammoth -- and if that's the case -- then Kucherov should be in the mix for the Norris Trophy. There is a great young core of forwards in Salt Lake City, and I think Kucherov would be a perfect fit alongside Logan Cooley, who is emerging as a franchise center.

Utah also has plenty of draft capital with which to work, and it's projected for just over $25 million in salary cap space next season. The Mammoth don't have any major pending free agents on their cap sheet, so they're a suitor capable of signing Kucherov to a long-term extension.

Allow me to get a little bold on the fifth and final destination. The Stars have already failed to sign 27-year-old winger Jason Robertson to a long-term extension once. The two sides agreed to a one-year deal worth $12 million prior to the season, but Robertson's future with the team is still very much in doubt. What if Dallas and Tampa Bay executed a true "hockey trade" -- one player for one player?

Dallas would get the better player in Kucherov, but there are no guarantees regarding an extension. The Stars are in win-now mode, and Kucherov could help them get over the Cup hump immediately. Tampa Bay would get a younger player in Robertson, and although he doesn't have the elite playmaking ability of Kucherov, he's still an exceptionally talented scorer. Perhaps the Bolts could get him to join the team's core and sign a multi-year contract. This deal could work for both sides.

#2553. Declan Rice confirms new Arsenal contract is 'on the horizon' as England star prepares to commit long-term future to Premier League champions

Declan Rice has handed Arsenal a massive boost by confirming that a new long-term contract at the Emirates Stadium is likely to be signed in the near future. The England international, who has been a transformative figure since his big-money move from West Ham, appears ready to commit the prime years of his career to Mikel Arteta's Premier League champions.

Rice arrived in north London from West Ham for £105 million in 2023, and his existing agreement runs until 2028, though Arsenal hold an option for an additional year.

Gunners manager Mikel Arteta has already stated it is "a matter of time" before the deal is finalised. Speaking to reporters in Madrid ahead of England's Nations League clash with Spain, Rice indicated he is eager to sign.

Reflecting on his career stability and the backing he receives at the Emirates Stadium, Rice explained why he wants to stay put.

"I've been extremely lucky that I've managed to play at such a consistent level throughout my career," the 27-year-old said. "I'm a player that always sets myself targets, always pushes for more. I've always been stable in the clubs I'm at. New contract hopefully on the horizon soon.

"I'm extremely lucky I'm at a club like Arsenal where the manager shows me so much trust, I've so many teammates who put so much energy and effort into me. I'm extremely lucky that I don't have to worry about that stuff. It makes playing football a lot easier."

Rice has played a pivotal role in ending Arsenal's 22-year wait for a Premier League crown and guiding the club to just their second Champions League final last term. He hopes England can replicate that collective spirit under Thomas Tuchel.

"What the manager has installed in us at Arsenal is to not have any fear," Rice said. "The progression in the Champions League over the last three years - quarterfinal, semifinal, final - coming to this stadium last year, we've been to the Bernabeu, Bayern Munich. The Arsenal of old may have struggled in those stadiums. Playing in that team now, putting on that shirt before that game, you know what you're going to get before you go out there.

"You're going to get a strong team, togetherness, we're going to run for each other, we're going to play forward, So I'm extremely lucky at the minute that I'm in a beautiful team with such great players and with a manager who is leading us and with players who listen to him and follows all his instructions. It is no surprise we're on the trajectory we're on at the minute. Long may it continue.

"That togetherness, that's what's building [with England]. Thomas is only short into his reign here at England. He's come in with the World Cup straight away and now playing the top teams in the Nations League. But you need time to time to build these things. Squads are constantly changing.

"So I think the biggest thing for me is constantly, every time we're in camp, build that togetherness when we're in training, build relationships and then take that into this kind of game tomorrow night and that's where you see where you're at as a group."

England face an immediate benchmark in Madrid as Tuchel continues to shape his squad against elite opposition following a rapid transition from the World Cup into the Nations League.

Fresh from Thursday's 2-1 victory over Croatia, Tuchel confirmed James Trafford will start in goal ahead of Jordan Pickford. The Three Lions are also bolstered by the return of Ezri Konsa and Djed Spence, who have both proven their fitness after missing the Croatia win.

He has reportedly instructed his agent to explore another loan move in January. Most recently, Sky Germany reported two concrete inquiries without naming the clubs.

#2550. Banton pushes case and bowlers sparkle for inconsistent England

England 355-6 (50 overs): Banton 121, Cox 67, Root 62

Australia 220 all out (44.3 overs): Green 64, Renshaw 63; Atkinson 4-28

England won by 135 runs; series level at 1-1

Tom Banton scored a century and Sonny Baker and Gus Atkinson impressed with the ball as England's wildly inconsistent one-day team hammered Australia to set up a series decider.

Banton scored a fine 121 – pushing his case for selection further with a second ODI hundred – in England's 355-6.

After being knocked over for 131 two days ago in Perth, England's total was their highest in one-day internationals in Australia.

And then their bowlers, who failed to defend 430 against Sri Lanka last month and were undone by an improbable last-wicket partnership against Pakistan, reduced Australia to 29-4 inside seven overs and easily closed out a 135-run victory.

The win ends a seven-match losing run against Australia across formats in Adelaide - and a run of six consecutive defeats by Australia in 50-over cricket away from home.

But, more significantly, it corrects their course after those damaging defeats against Sri Lanka, Pakistan and Australia and offers positives amid the frustrations going into the decider on Wednesday (03:30 GMT) in Hobart.

Will the real England please stand up? Before those defeats in Rawalpindi, Lahore and Perth, England had won three ODI series this year.

This win only adds to the feeling they are extremely difficult to figure out.

Banton was superb and, even more encouragingly, Atkinson and Baker were too.

This England team has often struggled for new-ball wickets and Baker, brought in for Jamie Overton in an attempt to correct that fault, found significant swing. He took the key wicket of Australia captain Mitchell Marsh, taken high at slip by a diving Joe Root, for two.

Atkinson used nip to nick off Travis Head for seven – the second match in a row he has dismissed the Australia left-hander – and also have both Cooper Connolly and Josh Inglis caught behind. Career-best figures of 4-28 are reward for good recent performance that have often gone unrewarded.

England were not perfect. They dropped four catches – first Inglis and then Matt Renshaw and Cameron Green, who made 63 and 64 respectively to drag out Australia's score.

But by the end, Sam Curran had taken two wickets in two balls, including bowling Jack Edwards with his moon ball, in a boost after his poor run.

Green was also out stumped when the ball deflected off Jordan Cox's shin and onto the stumps and Liam Dawson took 2-41 as he was preferred again to Adil Rashid.

These are the performances that suggest England can challenge at next year's World Cup, but plenty more are needed.

Banton's hundred follows his first against Sri Lanka in September [Getty Images]

Banton's chance as opener has come courtesy of Jacob Bethell's knee injury. In nine innings, he has scored four fifties and two hundreds. The spot should now be his going forward.

The 28-year-old right-hander was hit on the helmet on 10 by left-armer Spencer Johnson but afterwards attacked Adelaide's short square boundaries with his pull.

A partnership of 137 with Joe Root was steady and important – given Ben Duckett had slashed to point for nine and the recent memory of Perth.

It was Banton's hundred, 67 from 49 balls by Cox and 54 not out by Will Jacks that, with Australia's match-winner from the first ODI, Mahli Beardman, rested, took England to a dominant position, however.

Banton scored around the ground but the majority of his boundaries were pulls into or over the leg side [BBC]

Cox came in after captain Harry Brook, on five, deflected the ball onto his stumps when trying a ramp to push on the scoring. Jacks joined him when Banton holed out at deep square-leg after one too many of those pulls.

Cox and Jacks were scoring at a run a ball when taking England to 245-4 after 40 overs but together helped their side take 110 from the last.

Cox, after a run of lower scores as he fills in for Jos Buttler, drove, cut, scooped and pulled. A reverse scoop for four off Xavier Bartlett was outrageous.

He has one more chance in this series to push his case further - possibly more if Buttler does not recovery for the January series against South Africa.

"Banton has really found his flow for batting," former England captain Michael Vaughan said.

"I don't know who the person was to say 'you can open the batting in 50-over cricket, Tom' but it's been a tremendous move. He and Ben Duckett look a good combo.

"Banton seems to have all the time, all the strokes. He's got the pull shot, he's got the drive down the ground and he plays spin great. He hasn't looked like he's trying to hard to score runs, he's just batted."

#2547. Ex-Guardians catcher Bo Naylor testifies in defense of Emmanuel Clase, Luis Ortiz in MLB pitch-rigging trial

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Former Cleveland Guardians catcher Bo Naylor on Thursday testified in federal court that he perceived nothing untoward about disputed pitches thrown by former All-Star closer Emmanuel Clase and his former Guardians teammate Luis Ortiz, ESPN reports.

Naylor, who played five seasons for the Guardians, appeared as a witness for the defense in the ongoing federal trial in which prosecutors allege that Clase and Ortiz rigged multiple pitches for the benefit of co-conspiring bettors. In Clase's case, he's alleged to have done so in 17 games across a two-year period beginning in May 2023. Naylor, now a member of the Milwaukee Brewers, was catcher for some of Clase's disputed appearances during that span, including seven of the 18 pitches he's alleged to have rigged.

Naylor, a defense witness, was shown video replays of some of the pitches the government alleges were predetermined by Clase or Ortiz as part of the scheme. Naylor was behind the plate for many of them and said they looked like common sliders outside the strike zone. He said the scouting reports on the hitters Ortiz faced during the two pitches in question indicated that sliders low and away would be a "weapon."

In November 2025, Clase and Ortiz were indicted by the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of New York. According to the Department of Justice, both pitchers "agreed in advance with their co-conspirators to throw specific types of pitches and speeds of pitches." The Department of Justice alleged that the pair made at least $450,000 by rigging outings and throwing specific pitches to benefit bettors who wagered on the outcomes of those pitches.

Both Clase and Ortiz pleaded not guilty to those charges in November of last year. Clase and Ortiz have been on administrative leave since late June 2025 while Major League Baseball investigates. MLB has the authority to discipline the pitchers regardless of how the criminal trial plays out.

The pair could face up to 65 years in prison if convicted on the charges of wire fraud conspiracy, honest services wire fraud conspiracy, conspiracy to influence sporting contests by bribery, and money laundering conspiracy.

#2541. Giannis Antetokounmpo stunned by Doc Rivers' 'bitterness and pettiness' after former coach's criticism

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The Miami Heat have gotten off to a slow start to Giannis Antetokounmpo's first season in south Florida, which has led to plenty of discussion about Antetokounmpo's fit with Bam Adebayo and the challenges of building around Giannis.

Among those to chime in on the topic is Antetokounmpo's former coach, Doc Rivers, who struggled to get the most out of the star in Milwaukee and never got Antetokounmpo and Damian Lillard on the same page. Rivers recently offered some critiques of Antetokounmpo, noting he's a difficult star to coach because of his play style and a defiance about changing how he plays.

On Sunday, after the Heat beat the Kings, Antetokounmpo was taken aback when asked about the comments by his former coach.

"You have his number, right? You do. I know you do. You gotta go ask him why he thought that; that's on him," Antetokounmpo told The Athletic. "That's not on me. I gotta focus on my team and what I gotta do and how can I be better and how can I help the team. But like, goddamn. That's crazy. Never let bitterness and pettiness get in front of your goals and dreams, man. For every athlete out there, never let that [happen]. That's insane, but you gotta go ask him why he said what he said. Not me."

Rivers' tenure in Milwaukee was a disaster: he took over for Adrian Griffin in the middle of the 2023-24 season with the Bucks 30-13 and proceeded to go 97-103 in his three years with the Bucks. Given Rivers' history of shifting blame, Antetokounmpo can more easily brush aside his critique as Doc once again finding someone else to blame for his team's shortcomings.

However, while Rivers might not be an infallible messenger, he did have some interesting comments about the challenge of coaching Antetokounmpo this week on The Bill Simmons Podcast.

"He has this great passing ability, but he doesn't necessarily have super IQ at the same time," Rivers said. "It's really a strange thing. And he really has one way. Downhill, forceful. Every play, he wants to force it.

"There's times where I wish he'd do one thing. I wish he'd learn how to execute better," Rivers added. "He's one of those guys, you get a lot of them from the U.S., AAU guys, who have never needed to execute, because they can do it on their own. That doesn't help the team."

It's not surprising that Antetokounmpo would balk at those comments, but viewing from the outside, there certainly seems to be validity to at least some of what Rivers says. Questioning a player's IQ will always understandably irk them, but watching Antetokounmpo play with Lillard and now Adebayo, the criticism of him wanting to attack downhill and not adjusting his play style has been apparent for some time.

What might help the Heat the most here is that, for as stubborn as Antetokounmpo can be, he is also fueled by a desire to prove people wrong. While Rivers may have been unable to get Antetokounmpo to buy into changing his style while playing for him, criticizing the former MVP might lead Giannis to show he can adapt his style purely out of spite.

We've ranked the top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and built you a calendar of the important offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Friday's hot stove happenings.

The market for two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, far and away the offseason's best free agent, is already hot, according to the New York Post. Skubal is expected to sign in November, before the collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1, though a deal is not imminent. Talks are underway, however, and his market is moving.

Skubal is expected to sign a record contract at least in total value, and possibly in average annual value. Yoshinobu Yamamoto's $325 million deal with the Dodgers is the largest pitching contract ever given out. Max Scherzer and Justin Verlander's matching $43.3 million salaries with the Mets years ago set the record for the average annual value for a pitcher.

The Dodgers, Mets, Padres, Phillies, and Yankees are among the teams linked to Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato, reports the New York Post. Unless MLB and the MLBPA unexpectedly avoid a lockout, Sato must sign before the collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. Otherwise, he will return to the Hanshin Tigers for 2027.

We ranked Sato as the fourth-best free agent available this offseason, and the best available position player. He has significant power but also swing-and-miss and defensive concerns at third base, similar to Munetaka Murakami a year ago. Murakami slugged 35 home runs in only 127 games as a rookie this season, providing proof of concept for Sato.

The Nationals have signed center fielder Jacob Young to a four-year extension, reports FanSided. The deal is worth $23 million and includes an $8 million club option for a fifth year. The extension buys out Young's three arbitration years and one free agent year, with a club option for a second free agent year. He's now under Washington's control through 2031.

Young, 27, has always been a superlative defender. He unlocked a new level on offense this season, particularly in the second half, when he hit .301 with a .385 on-base percentage. Young had been speculated as a trade candidate since last offseason, but the new extension locks him in as part of Washington's long-term core.
